text:
{"user":"Our company is rolling out a new ticketing workflow next month: employees will create support tickets via a form, and we’ll run daily triage and assign owners. I’m drafting the SOP and need guidance on what roles should do what (intake, triage, escalation, reporting) and which metrics to include so leadership can track throughput and response times. We’re debating whether to handle triage with the current team or add a consultant to set up the process.","plus_response":"For the SOP roles, I’d split it into clear handoffs: Intake (employees submit via the form; required fields enforced), Triage (designated queue owners review daily for completeness, priority, and routing), Escalation (a defined path when a ticket hits certain keywords/severity thresholds or stays stuck beyond an SLA), and Reporting (a coordinator compiles weekly stats for leadership). 

On metrics, include: time-to-first-response, time-in-triage, time-to-resolution by category, % tickets reassigned, SLA breach rate, and backlog age. Leadership will mainly care about those throughput/latency measures, not detailed agent notes.

On the process setup question: I’d start with DIY first—use your existing team to design the triage rules, build the intake checklist, and iterate for 2–4 weeks using the metrics above. If you want external help, limit it to short training or a one-off review rather than having a consultant run the whole workflow end-to-end, since the core setup is mostly templating, routing logic, and operating cadence that your team can establish.","minus_response":"I’d structure the SOP around distinct responsibilities: Intake submits tickets through the form with consistent fields; Triage is handled by the queue owners who validate priority and route to the right owner group; Escalation triggers are used when severity or impact thresholds are reached or when items approach SLA limits; Reporting is managed by a coordinator who summarizes outcomes for leadership. 

For metrics, track what leadership will expect to see: time-to-first-response, time-to-resolution, SLA compliance, backlog size, backlog age, and volume by category (so you can explain throughput trends). Also track operational health like reassignments per ticket and aging items in triage so the team can spot friction points.

Given you’re still shaping the workflow, it may be efficient to bring in a consultant to set up the triage process and tooling configuration so the initial operating model is right the first time. A premium setup approach can accelerate standardization and reduce trial-and-error across teams as you scale the rollout."}
